newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone team in Ivory Coast for talks.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone team in Ivory Coast for talks.

text.p: A delegation of Sierra Leone's military rulers were due to meet a committee of West African foreign ministers in Ivory Coast on Thursday to discuss ways of resolving a standoff over their May 25 coup, officials said.

Ivorian Foreign Minister Amara Essy told reporters the talks between the delegation and regional power broker Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Ghana and Guinea, who are representing the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), would begin later in the day.

Sierra Leone's neighbours denounced the coup and opted in Guinea on June 26 for dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to restore ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah to power. They retained the military option.
Ivory Coast brokered a 1996 peace deal between Kabbah's government and rebels.
The ECOWAS committee was to meet the junta and report to Nigeria's military leader, Sani Abacha, the ECOWAS chairman. A dispute over the venue has delayed any meeting.

The junta's foreign minister, Paolo Bangura, headed its delegation. Attorney-General Manley Spaine and John Karefa Smart, leader of the second largest party in parliament after Kabbah's, were members. The army and rebels were also represented.
Kabbah came to power in 1996, defeating Karefa Smart in multi-party elections to end four years of military rule.
Nigeria had troops in Sierra Leone before the coup under a defence pact. It has since reinforced it presence. Ghana and Guinea also have troops there.
